n-k-k1-01.title: Four notes, one claim
n-k-k1-01.goal: Decide which class notes really support claim about timetable, and explain wetin differ for note wey no support am.
n-k-k1-01.material: For class chat, Minho write: ‘저는 화요일 오후에 한국어 수업이 있어요.’ (I have Korean class on Tuesday afternoon.) Jina wan check am, so she look at notes below. Note na proof only if day, time of day, and subject all match di claim.
n-k-k1-01.thinking.1: Check day, time and subject one by one
n-k-k1-01.prereq.1: Know days of week and 수업, 있어요/없어요, 오전/오후
n-k-k1-01.s.s1.prompt: Which notes support Minho claim? Choose all wey do.
n-k-k1-01.s.s1.hint.0: Break claim into three parts: day, morning or afternoon, and subject.
n-k-k1-01.s.s1.hint.1: Check every note against all three parts, no be only di part wey look familiar.
n-k-k1-01.s.s1.r.b: Only di day match. Time of day and subject different, so this note no talk about Korean class for afternoon.
n-k-k1-01.s.s1.r.c: Time and subject match, but di day na 수요일 (Wednesday), no be 화요일.
n-k-k1-01.s.s1.explain: A fully support di claim (Tuesday, afternoon, Korean). D support am too because Tuesday afternoon na one of di two days listed. B match only di day, and C match everything except di day, so neither be proof.
n-k-k1-01.s.s2.prompt: Choose ONE note wey no support di claim (B or C). Write sentence (English okay) to say wetin different between that note and claim.
n-k-k1-01.s.s2.hint.0: Put di note and claim side by side and read dem small piece by piece.
n-k-k1-01.s.s2.hint.1: Say wetin dey in di note, and wetin di claim get instead.
n-k-k1-01.s.s2.selfAssess.0: I name di exact part wey different?
n-k-k1-01.s.s2.selfAssess.1: I say wetin claim get and wetin note get instead?
n-k-k1-01.s.s2.model.0: Note C na for Wednesday, but di claim say Tuesday, so di day different.
n-k-k1-01.s.s2.model.1: 수요일이에요. Minho say 화요일, so di day no match.
n-k-k1-01.s.s2.model.2: Note B na English class for morning, but claim na about Korean class for afternoon.
n-k-k1-01.s.s2.model.3: For note C, di day different from di claim.
n-k-k1-01.s.s3.prompt: Later Jina find one more note: ‘화요일에는 한국어 수업이 없어요.’ E get words 화요일 and 한국어 수업. Wetin e do to di claim?
n-k-k1-01.s.s3.hint.0: Di note agree with claim, or e disagree?
n-k-k1-01.s.s3.hint.1: Ask whether di note fit still be true if di claim true.
n-k-k1-01.s.s3.o.a: E no talk about di claim, because e no give time of day.
n-k-k1-01.s.s3.r.a: Di note talk about whole Tuesday, so afternoon dey inside am too.
n-k-k1-01.s.s3.o.b: E support di claim, because 화요일 and 한국어 수업 both dey there.
n-k-k1-01.s.s3.r.b: Same words no enough. 없어요 mean ‘there is none,’ so di meaning na opposite.
n-k-k1-01.s.s3.o.c: E go against di claim: note say no Korean class dey on Tuesday.
n-k-k1-01.s.s3.o.d: E only show say class dey at different time.
n-k-k1-01.s.s3.r.d: Di note say no Korean class on Tuesday at all, no be say class dey at different time.
n-k-k1-01.s.s3.explain: You judge proof by wetin note talk, no be which words e contain. 있어요 mean ‘there is’, 없어요 mean ‘there is not’, so this note contradict di claim.

n-k-k1-04.title: Two stories about one phone call
n-k-k1-04.goal: Use particles in short sentences to figure out who do what, and change your judgment when second speaker disagree.
n-k-k1-04.material: Three classmates talk about yesterday. Sujin, Minsu and Jiyeon na friends. 불렀어요 mean ‘called (someone over).’ Somebody call somebody, but the three no agree. 제가 mean ‘I’ (person doing action). 안 와서요 mean ‘because he/she no come.’ Read each message and answer; next message go come after you answer.
n-k-k1-04.thinking.1: Change your judgment when new statements arrive
n-k-k1-04.thinking.2: Trust particles, no be word order
n-k-k1-04.prereq.1: Know 이/가 and 을/를 as simple markers, and 아니에요
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.prompt: Read each message, choose reading wey seem most likely, then continue.
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.hint.0: Find who get 이/가 and who get 을/를 in each sentence.
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.hint.1: No use word order alone; check small markers after names.
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.st.0.after: 지영이 na person wey call, and 민수를 na person wey dem call. Na Sujin version.
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Person marked with 이/가 (지영이) do di calling. 민수를 na person dem call.
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.st.0.r.c: 수진 na only person wey dey tell story here; no sentence say 수진 call anybody.
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.st.0.o.d: 지영 and 민수 call each other.
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.st.0.r.d: Sentence no talk say dem call each other; e name one caller.
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.st.1.after: 민수 (제가) say say e call 지영. That na opposite of Sujin story, so one of dem get am wrong or call happen two times.
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.st.1.r.a: Dem name different callers: for 수진 message 지영 call, for 민수 message 민수 call.
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.st.1.o.b: Dem disagree: caller and person wey receive call turn around.
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.st.1.o.c: 민수 only say e no vex.
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.st.1.r.c: ‘아니에요’ here mean ‘no, that no be so,’ and next sentence give his own version.
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.st.1.o.d: Dem dey talk about two different days.
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.st.1.r.d: Nothing say di days different; 민수 answer 수진 directly with ‘아니에요.’
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.st.2.ask: Whose story 지영 message support? (Word order different, but check markers.)
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.st.2.after: 지영 say 제가 (I) called 민수를. That support Sujin version. Two speakers (수진, 지영) now say 지영 call, and only 민수 say opposite.
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.st.2.r.a: For ‘민수를 제가 불렀어요’, 민수를 na person wey dem call, and 제가 na caller (지영 herself).
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.st.2.o.b: Neither story, because word order change.
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Word order no change roles. Markers 를 and 가 still show who call who.
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.st.2.r.d: Di two stories give opposite roles, so one message no fit support both.
n-k-k1-04.s.s1.reflect: Marker after name show role: 이/가 mark person doing action, 을/를 mark person action happen to. Word order fit change, but roles stay same. When two speakers disagree, compare who get which role.
n-k-k1-04.s.s2.prompt: Now tell friend wetin Jiyeon say happen. Write one polite Korean sentence: 지영 call 민수. Put 민수 first in sentence this time, and use correct markers.
n-k-k1-04.s.s2.hint.0: Decide who na caller and who receive call, then choose marker for each name.
n-k-k1-04.s.s2.hint.1: Which marker show person wey receive call? Put that name at start of sentence.
n-k-k1-04.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Which name get 가/이 in my sentence and which one get 를/을?
n-k-k1-04.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Roles stay same even though 민수 come first?

n-k-k1-02.title: Summary wey talk too much
n-k-k1-02.goal: Compare short summary with original notice, find lines wey change wetin e talk, and correct dem.
n-k-k1-02.material:
School trip notice dey below, then classmate summary for friend wey miss school.

[Notice]
소풍 안내
- 날짜: 다음 주 금요일
- 장소: 한강 공원
- 점심: 집에서 가져와요.
- 물: 학교에서 줘요.
- 비가 오면: 학교에서 영화를 봐요.

[Di classmate summary dey for next step.]
n-k-k1-02.thinking.1: Compare summary with source one line at a time
n-k-k1-02.s.s1.prompt: Summary na for friend wey miss school. Which lines say something different from notice? Choose one.
n-k-k1-02.s.s1.hint.0: Check summary one line at a time and find matching bullet in notice.
n-k-k1-02.s.s1.hint.1: For each line, ask: who give am, where, and when? Compare those details.
n-k-k1-02.s.s1.explain: Line 3 and line 5 wrong. Notice say bring lunch from home (집에서 가져와요), and when rain fall, class go watch film at school (학교에서 영화를 봐요). Lines 1, 2 and 4 match notice.
n-k-k1-02.s.s2.prompt: Rewrite wrong lines for summary so dem match notice. Use Korean.
n-k-k1-02.s.s2.hint.0: Find matching bullet in notice for each wrong line and compare details.
n-k-k1-02.s.s2.hint.1: Write each corrected line as one short sentence, copying details from notice.
n-k-k1-02.s.s2.selfAssess.0: My lunch line say who bring lunch and from where?
n-k-k1-02.s.s2.selfAssess.1: My rain line say where and wetin dem go do?
n-k-k1-02.s.s3.prompt: Classmate wan make summary shorter and leave out line about water. Na same mistake like wrong lines wey you find?
n-k-k1-02.s.s3.hint.0: Ask wetin different between leaving fact out and saying different fact.
n-k-k1-02.s.s3.hint.1: Read water line in summary again beside notice before you decide.
n-k-k1-02.s.s3.o.a: Yes, because summary must repeat every line from notice.
n-k-k1-02.s.s3.r.a: Summary fit be shorter than notice. Leaving something out no be same as changing am.
n-k-k1-02.s.s3.o.b: No. Leaving out a detail make am shorter; e only become wrong if e say something different.
n-k-k1-02.s.s3.o.c: Yes, because water important for trip.
n-k-k1-02.s.s3.r.c: Importance no matter here. Question na whether summary say something wey notice no talk.
n-k-k1-02.s.s3.o.d: No, because water line na one of wrong lines anyway.
n-k-k1-02.s.s3.r.d: Water line match notice; e no be one of wrong lines.
n-k-k1-02.s.s3.explain: Good short summary fit drop details, but e must not change dem. Lunch and rain lines change meaning because dem say something different from notice; dropping water line only leave out one detail.

n-k-k1-03.title: Wetin time movie fit start?
n-k-k1-03.goal: Find different movie start times wey meet every condition in message, including one condition e only imply.
n-k-k1-03.material:
Minjun send message after school:

‘수업이 두 시에 끝나요. 같이 영화 봐요! 영화는 두 시간이에요. 극장은 학교 옆에 있어요. 영화가 끝나면 집까지 한 시간 걸려요. 저는 여섯 시까지 집에 가야 해요.’

For this task, write time as decimal afternoon hours: 2.5 mean 2:30 and 3 mean 3:00 (all times afternoon). Use only whole and half hours.
n-k-k1-03.prereq.1: Know Korean clock hours (한 시, 두 시, ... 여섯 시) and 시간
n-k-k1-03.s.s1.prompt: Wetin ‘여섯 시까지 집에 가야 해요’ tell you about di time?
n-k-k1-03.s.s1.hint.1: Test your understanding with two arrival times (one earlier and one later) and see which meaning fit.
n-k-k1-03.s.s1.o.a: He must leave for home exactly at six o’clock.
n-k-k1-03.s.s1.r.a: ‘까지’ show a limit, no be when person must leave.
n-k-k1-03.s.s1.o.b: He must reach home by six at latest.
n-k-k1-03.s.s1.o.c: He go home when movie start.
n-k-k1-03.s.s1.r.c: Sentence talk about time he must be home, no be when movie start.
n-k-k1-03.s.s1.o.d: He must reach home after six o’clock.
n-k-k1-03.s.s1.r.d: That na opposite: minimum, no be limit.
n-k-k1-03.s.s1.explain: ‘-까지’ mark end of range: up to six o’clock. Reaching home earlier okay; later no okay.
n-k-k1-03.s.s2.prompt: Find 3 different movie start times wey work. s = movie start time.
n-k-k1-03.s.s2.hint.0: List every condition from message in your own words: start limit, movie length, journey, deadline.
n-k-k1-03.s.s2.hint.1: Choose start time, add movie length, then journey home, and compare with deadline.
n-k-k1-03.s.s2.hint.2: Try start time half hour later than last one wey work.
n-k-k1-03.s.s2.fail.c0: Use whole or half hours only (for example 3 or 3.5).
n-k-k1-03.s.s2.fail.c1: 수업이 두 시에 끝나요: movie no fit start before class finish.
n-k-k1-03.s.s2.ok.c2: He must be home by six.
n-k-k1-03.s.s2.fail.c2: Add movie (2 hours) and journey home (1 hour): he go reach after six.
n-k-k1-03.s.s2.explain: Movie take 2 hours and journey home take 1 hour, so start time plus 3 hours must no pass 6. Since class finish by 2, possible start times na 2, 2.5 and 3.
n-k-k1-03.s.s2.because.prompt: Explain in sentence (English okay) why movie wey start by 3:30 no go work.
n-k-k1-03.s.s2.because.hint.0: Add movie time and journey home, starting from 3:30.
n-k-k1-03.s.s2.because.hint.1: Compare arrival time with deadline for message.
n-k-k1-03.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: I include journey home in my reasoning?
n-k-k1-03.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: I show the sum (start + movie + journey) or talk say e go reach home too late?
n-k-k1-03.s.s2.because.model.0: 3:30 plus 2 hours na 5:30, then journey home take 1 more hour, so e go reach by 6:30, after 6.

n-k-k1-05.title: Test classmate rule
n-k-k1-05.goal: Test classmate general rule by finding your own counterexample, and explain how to tell di two cases apart.
n-k-k1-05.material:
Hana dey learn Korean. She write this for her notebook:

‘If Korean sentence end with -요, na question.’

She see these sentences for dialogue: ‘뭐 해요?’, ‘어디 가요?’ and ‘이거 얼마예요?’ All of dem end with -요 and na questions. Now test her rule.
n-k-k1-05.prereq.1: Know basic -요 sentences and question words 뭐, 어디
n-k-k1-05.s.s1.prompt: Which sentence below be counterexample, meaning sentence wey end in -요 but no be question?
n-k-k1-05.s.s1.hint.0: Counterexample must end in -요 and also show say rule no always true.
n-k-k1-05.s.s1.hint.1: Read wetin each sentence mean, no be only how e end.
n-k-k1-05.s.s1.r.a: This na question with word 뭐 (what), so e follow Hana rule.
n-k-k1-05.s.s1.r.b: This na statement, but e end in -니다, no be -요, so e no break rule about -요.
n-k-k1-05.s.s1.r.d: This na question with word 어디 (where), so e follow Hana rule.
n-k-k1-05.s.s1.explain: ‘저는 학생이에요.’ mean ‘I am a student.’ E end in -요 but na statement. One counterexample enough to show say general rule no true.
n-k-k1-05.s.s2.prompt: Write your own counterexample: one Korean sentence about YOUR OWN day or life (no reuse sentence above) wey end in -요 and tell something, no be question or invitation.
n-k-k1-05.s.s2.hint.0: Think of something you do, like, or get, and say am politely.
n-k-k1-05.s.s2.hint.1: End your sentence with polite -요 ending, but no use question word.
n-k-k1-05.s.s2.selfAssess.0: My sentence tell something instead of asking?
n-k-k1-05.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Korean speaker fit answer ‘I see’ instead of replying to question?
n-k-k1-05.s.s3.prompt: So how listener or reader fit tell question from statement when both end in -요? Give two clues (English okay).
n-k-k1-05.s.s3.hint.0: Think about wetin speaker or writer do differently when asking.
n-k-k1-05.s.s3.hint.1: Think about wetin di situation tell you and wetin reply speaker expect.
n-k-k1-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Each clue work both in speech and writing?
n-k-k1-05.s.s3.model.0: In writing, question mark dey; in speech, voice rise at the end. The situation too show am: speaker expect an answer.
n-k-k1-05.s.s3.model.1: Rising voice show question, while situation or whole-sentence meaning show whether person dey ask or tell.
